Passed 2025-05-15. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Creates civil and criminal liability for the unauthorized disclosure of intimate digital depictions, including deepfakes. Allows depicted individuals to sue for damages and injunctive relief. Makes certain disclosures a felony, with a higher class if the content could affect a governmental proceeding or facilitate violence.

Who it applies to

  • Any person who intentionally discloses an intimate digital depiction without the depicted individual's consent, where the person knows or recklessly disregards the lack of consent (39-17-1903(a)).
  • Any person who discloses, threatens to disclose, or solicits the disclosure of an intimate digital depiction with the intent to harass, annoy, threaten, alarm, or cause substantial harm to finances or reputation, or with actual knowledge or reckless disregard of harm (39-17-1906(a)).
  • Providers of interactive computer services, information services, or telecommunications services are not liable for certain good faith actions or third party content (39-17-1905, 39-17-1906(d)).

Effective date

July 1, 2025 (Section 3).

Key definitions

  • Consent: an affirmative, conscious, and voluntary authorization made by the individual free from force, fraud, misrepresentation, or coercion (39-17-1902(1)).
  • Deepfakes: videos, images, or audio files that have been generated or manipulated by artificial intelligence in order to realistically portray something that did not actually occur (39-17-1902(2)).
  • Depicted individual: an individual who, as a result of digitization or by means of digital manipulation, appears in whole or in part in an intimate digital depiction and who is identifiable by virtue of the person's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic, such as a unique birthmark or other recognizable feature, or from information displayed in connection with the digital depiction (39-17-1902(3)).
  • Digital depiction: a realistic visual depiction of an individual that has been created or altered using digital manipulation and includes stored data which is capable of conversion into a visual image (39-17-1902(4)).
  • Disclose: to transfer, publish, distribute, or make accessible (39-17-1902(5)).
  • Intimate digital depiction: a digital depiction of an individual that has been created or altered using digital manipulation and that appears to depict the uncovered genitals, pubic area, anus, or postpubescent female nipple of an identifiable individual; the display or transfer of bodily sexual fluids onto any part of the body of an identifiable individual or from the body of an identifiable individual; or an identifiable individual engaging in sexually explicit conduct (39-17-1902(6)).
  • Sexually explicit conduct: graphic sexual intercourse, including genital-genital, oral-genital, anal-genital, or oral-anal, whether between persons of the same or opposite sex, or lascivious simulated sexual intercourse where the genitals, breast, or pubic area of any person is exhibited; graphic or lascivious simulated bestiality, masturbation, or sadistic or masochistic abuse; or graphic or simulated lascivious exhibition of the anus, genitals, or pubic area of any person (39-17-1902(7)).

Obligations

  • To establish valid consent for disclosure, the consent must be set forth in an agreement written in plain language signed knowingly and voluntarily by the depicted individual, and the consent must include a general description of the intimate digital depiction and, if applicable, the visual work into which the digital depiction will be incorporated (39-17-1903(c)(2)).
  • An individual's consent to the creation of the intimate digital depiction does not establish that the individual consented to its disclosure (39-17-1903(c)(1)).

Prohibitions

  • Intentionally disclosing an intimate digital depiction without the consent of the depicted individual, where the person knows or recklessly disregards whether the individual has not consented (39-17-1903(a)).
  • Disclosing or threatening to disclose or soliciting the disclosure of an intimate digital depiction with the intent to harass, annoy, threaten, alarm, or cause substantial harm to the finances or reputation of the depicted individual (39-17-1906(a)(1)).
  • Disclosing or threatening to disclose or soliciting the disclosure of an intimate digital depiction with actual knowledge that, or reckless disregard for whether, such disclosure or threatened disclosure will cause physical, emotional, reputational, or economic harm to the depicted individual (39-17-1906(a)(2)).

Penalties and enforcement

A depicted individual may bring a civil action in an appropriate court and recover the defendant's monetary gain, actual damages including emotional distress or liquidated damages of $150,000, punitive damages under 29-39-104, and the cost of the action including reasonable attorney's fees and litigation costs; courts may order temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctions, or permanent injunctions to cease display or disclosure, may grant injunctive relief maintaining confidentiality of a plaintiff using a pseudonym, and may authorize in camera proceedings (39-17-1903(a), 39-17-1904(a)-(c), (e)). Criminal violations are a Class E felony, or a Class C felony if the creation, reproduction, or distribution of the intimate digital depiction could be reasonably expected to affect the conduct of any administrative, legislative, or judicial proceeding of a governmental agency, including the administration of an election, or to facilitate violence; prosecution under another criminal statute is not prohibited (39-17-1906(b), (e)). The text does not state which agency enforces criminal violations.

How it affects AI deployment

  • AI systems that generate or manipulate realistic videos, images, or audio files fall within the definition of deepfakes, and outputs that appear to depict intimate content fall within intimate digital depiction, so organisations deploying such AI may face liability for disclosure (39-17-1902(2), (6)).
  • Organisations must obtain written plain language consent signed by the depicted individual, including a general description of the intimate digital depiction and any visual work, before disclosing AI generated intimate content; consent to creation is not consent to disclosure (39-17-1903(c)).
  • Disclosing AI generated intimate digital depictions without consent can lead to civil damages, including $150,000 liquidated damages, and injunctions ordering the organisation to cease display or disclosure (39-17-1903(a), 39-17-1904(a)-(b)).
  • Disclosing, threatening to disclose, or soliciting disclosure of AI generated intimate digital depictions with prohibited intent or knowledge is a felony, and a Class C felony if the content could reasonably be expected to affect a governmental proceeding or facilitate violence (39-17-1906(a)-(b)).
  • Providers of interactive computer services, information services, or telecommunications services are not liable for good faith actions to restrict access or for third party content, but this immunity does not cover the provider's own creation or disclosure of intimate digital depictions (39-17-1905, 39-17-1906(d)).

Notable exemptions

  • An identifiable individual shall not bring a civil action for a disclosure the defendant can show was made in good faith to or by a law enforcement officer or agency in the course of reporting or investigating unlawful activity or unsolicited or unwelcome conduct, or as part of a legal proceeding (39-17-1903(d)(1)).
  • An identifiable individual shall not bring a civil action for a disclosure made in good faith and reasonably intended to assist the identifiable individual (39-17-1903(d)(2)).
  • Providers of interactive computer services, information services, or telecommunications services are not liable for any action voluntarily taken in good faith to restrict access to or availability of intimate digital depictions, any action taken to enable or make available technical means to restrict access, or any content provided by another person in violation of this part (39-17-1905, 39-17-1906(d)).

Compliance steps

  • Identify whether the organisation's AI systems can create or alter intimate digital depictions as defined by the statute (39-17-1902(6)).
  • Implement controls to prevent disclosure of intimate digital depictions without valid written consent (39-17-1903(a), (c)).
  • Obtain written plain language consent signed knowingly and voluntarily by the depicted individual, including a general description of the intimate digital depiction and the visual work if applicable, before any disclosure (39-17-1903(c)(2)).
  • Train personnel that consent to creation does not equal consent to disclosure and that disclaimers stating the depiction was unauthorized or that the individual did not participate are not defenses (39-17-1903(c)(1), 39-17-1904(f), 39-17-1906(c)).
  • If the organisation is a provider of interactive computer services, information services, or telecommunications services, establish good faith mechanisms to restrict access to or availability of intimate digital depictions to qualify for immunity (39-17-1905, 39-17-1906(d)).
  • Monitor for criminal exposure by ensuring the organisation does not disclose, threaten to disclose, or solicit disclosure with prohibited intent or knowledge, and escalate if content could affect a governmental proceeding or facilitate violence (39-17-1906(a)-(b)).

AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 28 and Title 39, Chapter 17, relative to the
 unauthorized use of deepfake or actual likeness.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 17, is amended by adding the
following as a new part:

 39-17-1901. Short title.

 This part is known and may be cited as the "Preventing Deepfake Images Act."

 39-17-1902. Part definitions.

 As used in this part:

 (1) "Consent" means an affirmative, conscious, and voluntary authorization
 made by the individual free from force, fraud, misrepresentation, or coercion;

 (2) "Deepfakes" means videos, images, or audio files that have been
 generated or manipulated by artificial intelligence in order to realisti cally portray
 something that did not actually occur;

 (3) "Depicted individual" means an individual who, as a result of digitization or
 by means of digital manipulation, appears in whole or in part in an intimate digital
 depiction and who is identifiable by virtue of the person's face, likeness, or other
 distinguishing characteristic, such as a unique birthmark or other recognizable
 feature, or from information displayed in connection with the digital depiction;

 (4) "Digital depiction" means a realistic visual depiction of an individual that
 has been created or altered using digital manipulation and includes stored data which
 is capable of conversion into a visual image;

 (5) "Disclose" means to transfer, publish, distribute, or make accessible;

 (6) "Intimate digital depiction" means a digital depiction of an individual that
 has been created or altered using digital manipulation and that appears to depict:

 (A) The uncovered genitals, pubic area, anus, or postpubescent
 female nipple of an identifiable individual;

 (B) The display or transfer of bodily sexual fluids:

 (i) Onto any part of the body of an identifiable individual; or

 (ii) From the body of an identifiable individual; or

 (C) An identifiable individual engaging in sexually explicit conduct; and

 (7) "Sexually explicit conduct" means graphic sexual intercourse, including
 genital-genital, oral-genital, anal-genital, or oral-anal, whether between persons of the
 same or opposite sex, or lascivious simulated sexual intercourse where the genitals,
 breast, or pubic area of any person is exhibited; graphic or lascivious simulated
 bestiality, masturbation, or sadistic or masochistic abuse; or graphic or simulated
 lascivious exhibition of the anus, genitals, or pubic area of any person.

 39-17-1903. Civil action - Consent.

 (a) Except as provided in subsection (d), an individual who is the subject of an
 intimate digital depiction that is intentionally disclosed without the consent of the individual,
 where such disclosure was made by a person who knows that, or recklessly disregards
 whether, the individual has not consented to such disclosure, may bring a civil action against
 that person in an appropriate court as set forth in§ 39-17-1904.

 (b) In the case of an individual who has not attained eighteen (18) years of age or is
 incompetent, incapacitated, or deceased, the legal guardian of the individual or
 representative of the individual's estate, another family member, or any other person
 appointed as suitable by the court, may assume the individual's rights under this section, but
 in no event may the defendant be named as such representative or guardian.

 (c) For purposes of an action under this section:

 (1) An individual's consent to the creation of the intimate digital depiction does
 not establish that the individual consented to its disclosure; and

 (2) Consenl is deemed validly given only if:

 (A) The consent is set forth in an agreement written in plain language
 signed knowingly and voluntarily by the depicted individual; and

 (B) The consent includes a general description of the intimate digital
 depiction and, if applicable, the visual work into which the digital depiction will
 be incorporated.

 39-17-1904. Damages - Equitable relief - Preservation of anonymity - Exceptions -
Disclaimers.

 (a) In a civil action filed under this part, an individual may recover any of the following:

 (1) An amount equal to the monetary gain made by the defendant from the
 creation, development, or disclosure of the intimate digital depiction;

 (2) Either of the following:

 -'(A) The actual damages sustained by the individual as a result of the
 intimate digital depiction, including damages for emotional distress; or

 (B) Liquidated damages in the amount of one hundred fifty thousand
 dollars ($150,000);

 (3) Punitive damages, pursuant to§ 29-39-104; and

 (4) The cost of the action, including reasonable attorney's fees and other
 litigation costs reasonably incurred.

 (b) In a civil action filed under this part, a court may, in addition to any other relief
 available at law, order equitable relief, including a temporary restraining order, a preliminary
 injunction, or a permanent injunction ordering the defendant to cease display or disclosure of
 the intimate digital depiction.

 (c) In ordering relief under this section, the court may grant injunctive relief
 maintaining the confidentiality of a plaintiff using a pseudonym.

 (d) An identifiable individual shall not bring an action for relief under this section
 relating to:

 (1) A disclosure the defendant can show was made in good faith:

 (A) To or by a law enforcement officer or agency in the course of
 reporting or investigating:

 (i) Unlawful activity; or

 (ii) Unsolicited or unwelcome conduct; or

 (B) As part of a legal proceeding; or

 (2) A disclosure made in good faith and reasonably intended to assist the
 identifiable individual.

 (e) A court may authorize an in camera proceeding under this part.

 (f) It is not a defense to an action under this section that there is a disclaimer stating
 that the intimate digital depiction of the depicted individual was unauthorized or that the
 depicted individual did not participate in the creation or development of the material.

 39-17-1905. Limitations.

 For purposes of this part, a provider of an interactive computer service, as defined in
 47 U.S.C. § 230, or an information service or telecommunications service, as defined in 47
 U.S.C. § 153, is not liable on account of:

 (1) Any action voluntarily taken in good faith to restrict access to or availability
 of intimate digital depictions;

 (2) Any action taken to enable or make available to information content
 providers or other persons the technical means to restrict access to intimate digital
 depictions; or

 (3) Any content provided by another person in violation of this part.

 39-17-1906. Criminal action for intimate digital depictions - Penalty- Limitations.

 (a) It is an offense to disclose or threaten to disclose or solicit the disclosure of an
 intimate digital depiction:

 (1) With the intent to harass, annoy, threaten, alarm, or cause substantial
 harm to the finances or reputation of the depicted individual; or

 (2) With actual ~nowledge that, or reckless disregard for whether, such
 disclosure or threatened disclosure will cause physical, emotional, reputational, or
 economic harm to the depicted individual.

 (b) A violation of subsection (a):

 (1) Is a Class E felony; or

 (2) Is a Class C felony, in the case of a violation in which the creation,
 reproduction, or distribution of the 'intimate digital depiction could be reasonably
 expected to:

 (A) Affect the conduct of any administrative, legislative, or judicial
 proceeding of a governmental agency, including the administration of an
 election; or •

 (B) Facilitate violence.

 (c) It is not a defense to prosecution under this section that there is a disclaimer
 stating that the intimate digital depiction of the depicted individual was unauthorized or that
 the depicted individual did not participate in the creation or development of the material.

 (d) For purposes of this section, a provider of an interactive computer service, as
 defined in 47 U.S.C. § 230, or an information service or telecommunications service, as
 defined in 47 U.S.C. § 153, is not liable on account of:

 ( 1) Any action voluntarily taken· in good faith to restrict access to or availability
 of intimate digital depictions;

 (2) Any action taken to enable or make available to information content
 providers or other persons the technical means to restrict access to intimate digital
 depictions; or

 (3) Any content provided by another person in violation of this section.

 (e) This section does not prohibit prosecution and conviction under another criminal
 statute.

 SECTION 2. The headings in this act are for reference purposes only and do not constitute a
part of the law enacted by this act. However, the Tennessee Code Commission is requested to
include the headings in any compilation or publication containing this act.

 SECTION 3. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
